skill.name: run-nx-generator
skill.description: Run Nx generators in a monorepo while prioritizing workspace-plugin generators and verification steps.
skill.summary: Guides generator selection, schema checks, dry-runs, and post-generation verification for Nx workspaces.
skill.author: nrwl

security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown backtick and code block detections around documented Nx commands, not Ruby shell execution. The skill does intentionally guide shell-based Nx workflows, so users should review generated commands and workspace changes before execution. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or hidden malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are central to the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to show the exact Nx, test, and formatting commands before running them.

remediation.issue: Generator options can change many workspace files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the dry-run guidance prominent and require review of generated files before applying changes.

remediation.issue: Workspace-plugin generators may contain local project logic.
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to run generators only from trusted workspaces with reviewed dependencies.

content.value_statement: Nx workspaces often have several generator choices, including internal workspace-plugin tools. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code choose, run, and verify the right generator.
actual_capabilities: Prioritizes workspace-plugin generators before core Nx generators.
Guides users to inspect generator schemas with the Nx MCP schema tool.
Provides a standard workflow for running Nx generators with paths and options.
Recommends dry-run previews before applying generated changes.
Recommends affected tests, formatting, file review, and separate generator commits.
Includes examples for Maven version bumps and create-nodes plugin creation.
limitations: Requires an Nx workspace with the needed generators and dependencies installed.
Does not validate the internal behavior of local workspace-plugin generators.
Generated files may still need manual review, edits, and test fixes.
Uses shell commands, so users should confirm commands before execution.

use_cases.title: Scaffold Workspace Features
use_cases.description: Use the preferred workspace generator before falling back to standard Nx generators.

use_cases.title: Create Nx Plugins
use_cases.description: Generate create-nodes plugins with a repeatable schema-first workflow.

use_cases.title: Automate Version Updates
use_cases.description: Apply internal generators for Maven plugin version bumps and related workspace changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Generator
prompt_templates.prompt: Use run-nx-generator to identify the best workspace-plugin generator for adding a new React library.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Generator Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use run-nx-generator to inspect the schema for a Node library generator and prepare a dry-run plan for a billing library.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Verify Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use run-nx-generator to create a create-nodes plugin named asset-indexer, then list the files to review and tests to run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Version Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use run-nx-generator to plan a Maven plugin version bump to 0.0.10 for Nx 22.1.0-beta.7. Prefer workspace-plugin generators.

output_examples.input: I need a new Node library in an Nx workspace.
output_examples.output: The skill checks workspace-plugin options first, then recommends a Node generator only if no internal generator fits.

output_examples.input: I want to update a Maven plugin version.
output_examples.output: The skill points to the workspace-plugin version bump workflow and asks for the target plugin and version values.

output_examples.input: I generated files and need confidence before committing.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends reviewing generated files, running affected tests, formatting changes, and keeping the generator commit separate.

best_practices: Start with workspace-plugin generators and inspect the schema before choosing options.
Use dry-run previews and review generated files before applying changes.
Run affected tests and format generated files after generation.
anti_patterns: Running a generator before checking its schema or workspace-specific alternative.
Mixing generator output with unrelated manual edits in one commit.
Skipping review because a generator produced the files automatically.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose, run, and verify Nx generators in a monorepo.

faq.question: Does it prefer internal generators?
faq.answer: Yes. It tells the agent to check workspace-plugin generators before core Nx generators.

faq.question: Can it inspect generator options?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the agent to use the Nx MCP schema tool for generator options.

faq.question: Does it apply changes automatically?
faq.answer: It guides generator execution, but users should review commands and generated files first.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users do after generation?
faq.answer: They should review files, run affected tests, format changes, and commit generator output separately.
